title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page gives the existence half of Th. 1.1 (previous page). Setting: X and Y are smooth connected varieties over an algebraically closed field k, of dimensions n and m. Z is an m-dimensional cycle (codimension n) on X×Y. The claim is that there is a unique homomorphism of abelian varieties u_Z : A_Y → A_X such that S_X(Z(𝔫)) = u_Z(S_Y(𝔫)) for every degree-0 zero-cycle 𝔫 on Y with Z(𝔫) defined. Here S denotes the Albanese summation map. The previous page also asserts that u_Z depends only on the numerical class of Z.

Construction, in modern terms:
(1) Let φ_X : X → A^1_X = X' be the canonical map to the Albanese torsor (the 'homogeneous' Albanese, a principal homogeneous space under A_X). Push Z forward: Z' = (φ_X × id_Y)_*Z ∈ Cyc_m(X'×Y).
(2) Let B = Pic^{00}_{A^1_X/k} ≅ Pic^0_{A_X/k} = A_X^∨, the dual abelian variety. Pullback φ_X^* identifies it canonically with Pic^{00}_{X/k}, the reduced Picard variety of X. This is the duality between Albanese and Picard varieties.
(3) Let Θ ∈ Pic(B×X') be the universal (Poincaré) class. Let Θ' be its pullback to B×X'×Y, and θ' the numerical class of Θ'. Let Z'' = B×Z' on B×X'×Y, with numerical class 𝔷''; this depends only on the numerical class of Z.
(4) With π : B×X'×Y → B×Y the projection, set c = π_*(𝔷''·θ'). Dimension count: (b+m) − 1 inside a (b+m)-dimensional space, so c is a numerical class of divisors on B×Y.
(5) Continued on the next page: a numerical divisor class on B×Y determines a divisorial-correspondence class c'. The reason is that the group of divisorial correspondences, Hom(A_Y, Pic^0_B), is torsion-free, and its component of NS(B×Y) is detected numerically. So c' gives A_Y → Pic^0_{B/k}, and Cartier biduality identifies Pic^0_{B/k} with A_X. This yields u_Z, manifestly depending only on the numerical class of Z.

In effect, this is the family version of the action Z^* : Pic^0_X → Pic^0_Y, D ↦ pr_{Y*}(Z·pr_X^*D), applied to the universal divisor over B = Pic^0_X. It is then dualized. The compatibility with S (Lemma 1.4) is deferred to the next page.

Purpose: an intersection-theoretic lemma within the 1965–71 notes on the standard and Hodge/Tate conjectures. It shows that the degree-1 (Albanese / h^1) action of correspondences factors through numerical equivalence.
errors: The word 'projectives' was crossed out in Th. 1.1, but the construction needs properness. The pushforward (φ_X×id)_* requires φ_X proper, i.e. X complete. Numerical equivalence, and its compatibility with π_* and with pr_B^*, requires Y (hence X'×Y and B×X'×Y) complete. Without completeness, 'classe d'équivalence numérique' is not well defined. So X and Y must be assumed proper (projective).

The step 'numerical class of divisors on B×Y, donc a divisorial correspondence class' is stated without justification on this page. It is correct: the Hom(A_Y, B^∨) part of NS(B×Y) is torsion-free and determined numerically, by Matsusaka-type homological ≡ numerical mod torsion for divisors. Still, it is the non-trivial point of the 'depends only on numerical class' claim.
Minor notational slip: the final formula writes Θ where the numerical class θ' of the pulled-back Θ' is meant.

ideas.what: Homomorphism of Albanese varieties induced by an algebraic correspondence, characterized by compatibility with the Albanese map on zero-cycles
ideas.modern_name: Action of correspondences on Albanese/Picard varieties (functoriality of h^1 motives)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (Variétés abéliennes et courbes algébriques, 1948), Matsusaka, Lang (Abelian Varieties, 1959)
ideas.where_published: Treated in Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968) in Grothendieck's program; not known in Grothendieck's own published texts

ideas.what: Construction via the Poincaré bundle on (dual Albanese)×(Albanese torsor) plus Cartier biduality: Z acts on the universal divisor and the result is dualized
ideas.modern_name: Pic^0/Albanese duality and the Poincaré bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil, Cartier, Nishi (biduality); Grothendieck (Picard scheme, FGA)
ideas.where_published: FGA exposés on the Picard scheme (Pic^0, Pic^τ, Albanese duality), as background tools

ideas.what: The induced map on Albanese varieties depends only on the numerical equivalence class of the correspondence
ideas.modern_name: Homological = numerical equivalence on the h^1 ⊗ h^{2d-1} Künneth part; numerically trivial correspondences act trivially on Pic^0/Alb
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published works as far as known; standard in the literature on standard conjectures (Kleiman 1968, 1994)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard proof that correspondences act on Albanese varieties through numerical equivalence. It is done via the Poincaré bundle and Cartier biduality, which is classical (Weil, Matsusaka, Lang) and was made systematic in Kleiman's 1968 exposition of Grothendieck's standard-conjecture program. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's own working notes for that program, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit [-Θ-] Θ' la classe de diviseurs': the second symbol is a lowercase/script θ', i.e. the numerical class of Θ'. It is distinct from Θ'.
'et soit de [-‾-] 𝔷''': the struck symbol looks like '≡' (or a struck 'π'), not an overline.
'Soit [-π-]' before the definition of π: the struck text appears to be 'πr' or 'π:'.
In the formula c = π_*(𝔷''·Θ), the second factor should be read as the numerical class θ' of Θ'.
